contract_shape.parameter_source: For each SDK-backed entry, sdk_resource plus sdk_method identifies the exact openai==3.17.0 generated signature; extra_headers, extra_query, extra_body, and timeout are transport escape hatches, not product parameters.
contract_shape.response_source: The pinned SDK return annotation and Pydantic response models are canonical for SDK-backed entries; binary content operations return streamed bytes and events.stream returns AgentSessionEvent SSE objects.
contract_shape.error_source: Documented cross-operation validation and lifecycle failures are recorded in behaviors and per-operation remaining fields. The public Agents guide/reference snapshot does not publish a complete per-operation error matrix, so absent detail remains an explicit coverage gap rather than an inferred contract.
contract_shape.validation: tests/sdk_inventory.py resolves every SDK-backed method, HTTP verb, path, Agents beta header, and tracked resource method; strict fixtures validate representative Agent and AgentSession response objects.

behaviors.current: Official-style routes require a bearer token and accept the beta header.
behaviors.remaining: Match header requirements, project permission failures, and documented error bodies across every operation.

behaviors.current: Saved and inline fields preserve omitted values, replace supplied objects, and reset nulls. Provider requests verify effort, summary, text, and auto/default/flex/priority tiers across cold resume.
behaviors.remaining: Session updates change only model, effort, and tier for later turns; prototype limits and provider-specific model compatibility remain.

behaviors.current: Agent metadata enforces 16 string pairs, 64-character keys, 512-character values; omitted preserves, null/empty clears, supplied objects replace. SDK covers unicode limits and invalid updates.
behaviors.remaining: Agents and sessions share one validator; extend it to remaining metadata-bearing resources and project scope.

behaviors.current: Agents, sessions, items, and turns support after/order/limit with exclusive cursors that reject unknown or deleted IDs; sessions filter by agent_id.
behaviors.remaining: Apply stable created_at plus ID ordering, exclusive cursors, ownership validation, defaults, filters, and 1..100 limits to every list operation; environment files use opaque page tokens.

behaviors.current: Batches of 1-32 events are validated whole, then run in order: tool results plus at most one message or cancel. Messages carry text and data-URL images. Idempotency-Key is scoped to the session, retained 24 hours, replays stored outcomes, rejects different reuse (400) and concurrent use (409), and reports interrupted dispatch as unknown (409) without re-running.
behaviors.remaining: The public docs define neither batch nor idempotency semantics; these are local decisions pending an upstream contract. Initial input for non-none environments waits for G09.

behaviors.current: Streams are live-only and close on lag (1,024-event buffer), backend loss, or session deletion. Items follow the SDK added/part/delta/done order; terminal turns close unfinished items as incomplete; a documented subscribe/read/merge recovery reproduces saved items.
behaviors.remaining: Environment/subagent event families and real-provider ordering evidence; never promise replay.

behaviors.current: Pending calls; string or input_text/input_image content-part results; failures as error; 10,000-byte result text (below Codex's truncation); identical-retry receipts; racing results resolve once (409 for the loser); late results after cancellation conflict; batched results; the SDK-recognized pending-call race error; loss-to-unresolved behavior.
behaviors.remaining: Deferred functions with tool search, which needs worker-reported model support; the public docs publish no result size limit, so 10,000 bytes is a local decision.

behaviors.current: All pinned SDK tool configuration variants persist and round trip. Public HTTP MCP servers with service origin execute as session-scoped Codex servers with allowed_tools, non-secret headers, bearer credentials from session vaults, required-server failure as a failed turn, and an egress policy that refuses non-public addresses unless the operator allows the host. Other unsupported execution is rejected explicitly.
behaviors.remaining: Stdio and environment-origin MCP (G09), inline MCP authorization, request metadata, web search and deferred functions/tool search (need worker-reported provider/model support), and programmatic calling (G08).

behaviors.current: multi_agent enables Codex's V2 multi-agent runtime with max_concurrent_subagents + 1 threads (the root counts). Subagents are registered from spawn activity, emit subagent.created, have no function tools, and their turns and items are recorded apart from root history and stream tagged with subagent_id. Their usage counts toward the session. Deletion refuses while a subagent is active. Cancellation interrupts running subagent turns, and restarted sessions resume existing subagents under the same IDs.
behaviors.remaining: Subagent task text/model in call items, and wait_for_subagents/close/resume items and closed status, which Codex V2 does not report.

behaviors.current: Official-style sessions accept environment none; the prototype has a non-contract read-only local mode.
behaviors.remaining: Implement self-hosted attachment first, then managed provisioning; five-minute input-time connection wait, no blind command/input replay, and separate session/compute ownership.
Implement packages, setup commands, files, env restrictions, skills/plugins, templates, capability directories, and network enabled/disabled/restricted with 1..100 exact hosts.

Enforce 50 creation files, 5 MiB inline each, 10 MiB inline total, 50 MiB Files API source, 200 MiB artifact, and 500 MiB published-output total; stream transfers and preserve artifact/session lifetime rules.

behaviors.current: Vault and credential metadata live in SQLite. Secret values are encrypted (age with scrypt) under an operator-supplied passphrase in the data directory, and are never returned, stored in public records, or sent to the model. Without a passphrase, credential operations return 501. Sessions attach vault_ids; each service-origin HTTP MCP server takes the credential its credential_id names or the only credential for its URL, and several matches are rejected. Each session snapshots its secrets at creation, so rotation and deletion affect only newer sessions. static_bearer tokens and mcp_oauth access tokens become the server's Authorization header.
behaviors.remaining: environment_variable credentials and networking restrictions (need G09 environments), OAuth token refresh, inline MCP authorization, project scoping, and external key management.

behaviors.current: Webhook endpoints are managed through the SDK's /webhook_endpoints API, accepting the five agent.session.* event types. Signing secrets are encrypted in the vault store and returned only at creation and rotation. Test deliveries are signed with the Standard Webhooks scheme the SDK verifies, go only to https public addresses (or operator-allowed hosts), connect to the checked addresses, and do not follow redirects. Session status changes queue deliveries in the same transaction (outbox), delivered at least once with a stable webhook-id, retried with exponential backoff for 72 hours across restarts.
behaviors.remaining: Environment connection data in created and action_required events (G09); ordering is not guaranteed after a failed attempt.

behaviors.current: Turn and session usage are summed from increases in each thread's cumulative Codex token totals, so replays and repeated updates are not double-counted; subagent turns carry their own usage and count toward the session; null until reported; cached and reasoning tokens are included in input and output.
No public implementation and no Python SDK 3.17.0 resource method.
behaviors.remaining: Implement paginated OTLP JSON via raw HTTP and retain a fixture until SDK support exists.

behaviors.current: Managed startup/shutdown and completed-session resume work. A crashed managed worker restarts with bounded backoff while durable reads keep serving; backend generations are fenced; turns and function results lost to a disconnect are reconciled from rollout history; a worker orphaned by an API crash is reclaimed on Unix.
behaviors.remaining: Cover Windows orphan containment, the spawn-to-record window, and environment failure (G09). Lost function waiters become unresolved rather than re-driven.

behaviors.current: Provider examples were inventoried as consumers of the common self-hosted contract, not extra public endpoints.
behaviors.remaining: Validate the common executor attachment and lifecycle against at least one actual provider; provider selection and billing remain separate decisions.

compatibility_change_process: Pin a new SDK/docs review date in a dedicated change; never silently reinterpret the 3.17.0 baseline.
